title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Customer Comms
author: Miguel Santos
summary: A consolidated, production-facing playbook describing incident lifecycle, roles and responsibilities, standardized runbooks, postmortem process, on-call rotations, game-day guidance, and canonical status page / customer communication templates.
content:
Purpose

This playbook standardizes how Redwood Inference detects, responds to, and learns from incidents that affect availability, correctness, or security of the inference platform. It combines the incident process, runbook templates, postmortem guidelines, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates.

Scope

- Applies to all production services and infra managed by Redwood Inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane, and supporting infra).
- Includes incidents impacting customer-facing latencies, errors, data integrity, security incidents, and major operational degradations.

Definitions and Severity Levels

1) Sev 1 (P0) — Major outage
- Symptoms: Global or region-wide service unavailability, customer API errors > 50% for > 5 minutes, critical security incident with confirmed exfiltration.
- Target response: acknowledge within 5 minutes, mitigation plan within 15 minutes.

2) Sev 2 (P1) — Major degradation
- Symptoms: Significant functionality degraded for many customers (e.g., model serving latency > SLA for >10% of requests across a region), or sustained high error rates for key endpoints.
- Target response: acknowledge within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 60 minutes.

3) Sev 3 (P2) — Limited impact
- Symptoms: Partial degradation affecting subset of customers or non-critical functionality, intermittent errors.
- Target response: acknowledge within 4 hours, remediation tracked in backlog.

4) Sev 4 (P3) — Minor issue / operational task
- Symptoms: Low impact bugs, documentation gaps, one-off customer incidents.
- Target response: handled as usual engineering work.

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step)

1) Detection & Triage
- Monitoring alert or external report triggers incident.
- Pager duty/on-call engineer acknowledges alert and sets incident severity.
- Use incident Slack channel #incident-{id} and runbook checklist.

2) Mobilize & Communicate
- Primary on-call owns coordination.
- For Sev 1/2 escalate to SOC (if security), SRE lead, and Product Ops.
- Create incident timeline document in the incident doc template (link in runbook).

3) Contain & Mitigate
- Run relevant runbooks (see section Runbook Templates).
- Apply mitigations that minimize customer impact (fallbacks, traffic routing, throttles, autoscaling).

4) Restore Service
- Restore customer-facing service to acceptable SLOs.
- Validate traffic and monitor for regression for 30+ minutes.

5) Postmortem & Remediate
- For Sev 1/2 incidents, complete a written postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and publish within 7 business days.
- Track follow-up actions (P0/P1 remediation) in issue tracker with owners and due dates.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Primary On-Call (SRE/Platform): initial acknowledgement, triage, runbook execution, incident doc updates, customer comms draft.
- Secondary On-Call: backup for escalations and tactical tasks, takes over if primary unavailable.
- Service Owner (team owning the impacted service): technical lead for root cause, implements fixes and remediation.
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned for Sev 1/2 to coordinate cross-team activity and communications.
- Communications Lead: drafts public status updates and customer emails with Product Ops / Support.
- Security Lead: engaged immediately for any suspected security incidents.

On-call Rotations & Expectations

- Rotation cadence: Weekly rotations for production SREs and platform on-call (7 days).
- Handoff checklist: previous on-call must publish a handoff note listing outstanding incidents, ongoing mitigations, and scheduled maintenance.
- Time zone coverage: primary coverage is NA/EU daytime; we maintain partial APAC overlap via follow-the-sun volunteers and on-call overlap hours.
- Escalation path: primary -> secondary (15 min) -> on-call manager (30 min) -> director (60 min).
- Overtime/backfill: teams coordinate with People Ops to manage post-incident rest/rebalance.

Runbook Templates (standardized, copyable)

Each runbook must contain the following fields as plain text to be pasted into an incident doc:

- Runbook name
- Service(s) affected
- Symptoms / alert patterns
- Required access and credentials (role names, k8s namespaces, links to playbooks)
- Immediate safe actions (ordered list)
- Diagnostic commands and sample queries (CLI and Grafana/Datadog queries)
- Common root causes and known mitigations
- Rollback steps for recent changes (if applicable)
- Post-action verification steps
- Owner and last updated date

Example runbook excerpt:

Runbook name: API high-5xx-rate
Service: inference-api (hosted-frontends)
Symptoms: 5xx rate > 10% sustained for 5+ minutes across frontends; latency increase > 2x baseline
Immediate actions:
1) Acknowledge alert and open incident channel.
2) Check deployment health: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-frontend
3) Check recent deploys in the last 30 minutes (CI/CD dashboard).
4) If recent deploy found, rollback to prior revision: deploy rollback CLI (link).
5) If no deploy, scale up frontends by +2 pods and monitor.

Diagnostic queries (Datadog):
- apm.service.error_rate{service:inference-api}.rollup(sum, 60)
- nginx.request.count{status:5xx}.as_rate()

Post-incident: run load tests against canary cluster and validate SLO compliance.

Postmortem Process & Template

Postmortem goals: capture timeline, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and follow-ups. Focus on facts, avoid finger-pointing, and assign measurable remediation.

Required sections (for Sev 1/2):
- Title, date, incident ID, severity, and author
- Summary (one-paragraph impact summary)
- Timeline (minutes resolution for first 2 hours, then coarser)
- Root cause analysis (5 whys + evidence)
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations + long-term fixes)
- Action owners and due dates (tracked in issue tracker)
- Lessons learned and prevention suggestions
- Severity and detection improvements (monitoring, alerts)
- Linked playbooks, dashboards, and code changes

Publishing & Review cadence:
- Draft within 72 hours.
- Peer review by Service Owner, SRE, and Product Ops within 5 business days.
- Final publish and review with leadership if Sev 1.

Game Days & Readiness Exercises

Purpose: validate runbooks, cross-team coordination, and restore procedures without customer impact.

Planning checklist:
1) Define scope and failure modes (e.g., AZ outage, KV cache corruption, model rollback).
2) Schedule a dry-run and invite Service Owners, SREs, Product Ops, and Support.
3) Prepare game-day incident doc template and measurement goals.
4) Execute scenario with intentional faults and time-boxed recovery steps.
5) Capture stopwatch timings for detection, mitigation, and restore.
6) Run a short retro and assign follow-ups.

Frequency: At least quarterly for each critical platform domain; post-major-release game day for 2 weeks after rollout.

Status Page & Customer Communication Templates

Guiding principles:
- Be timely, transparent, and factual. Avoid speculation.
- Indicate impact, affected regions/services, mitigation status, and next steps.
- Use consistent taxonomy: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved.

Status page entries (example):
Title: Increased inference API errors in eu-central-1
Status: Identified
Impact: Customers in eu-central-1 may see 5xx errors or latency > 3x baseline for text-generation and chat endpoints.
Updated: 2026-02-10T15:23Z
Next update: 2026-02-10T15:43Z\nCustomer email template (short):
Subject: Incident: Inference API errors in eu-central-1 (ongoing)
Hi {Customer},
We are aware of an ongoing issue impacting inference API requests for customers in eu-central-1. We are actively investigating and have mitigations in place to reduce impact. We will provide updates every 20-30 minutes or as material changes occur.
If you have any critical workloads, please reply to this email and our support team will prioritize assistance.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

Internal comms template (Slack pinned message):
- Incident ID: {INC-YYYYMMDD-###}
- Severity: Sev 1 / Sev 2
- Summary: short summary line
- Primary on-call: @name (contact)
- IC: @name (if assigned)
- Current status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved
- Next update ETA: HH:MM UTC
- Runbook link: {link}

Metrics, SLOs, and Post-incident KPIs

Track the following for each incident:
- Time to acknowledge (TTA)
- Time to mitigation (TTM) — first action meaningfully reducing customer impact
- Time to restore (TTR) — service restored to SLO thresholds
- Number of customers impacted and duration (customer-minutes)
- Post-incident action completion rate and mean time to close follow-ups

Operational Requirements & Tooling

- Incident tracking: use company incident system (incident-{id}) and attach the incident doc.
- PagerDuty for escalation and on-call paging.
- Slack incident channels prefixed with #incident-
- Datadog for metrics/APM, Grafana dashboards for visualization, and Sentry for error traces.
- Internal runbook repository (confluence + runbooks stored as JSON in repo) with last-updated date.

Ownership, Onboarding & Training

- Every new SRE/Platform hire must complete a 2-week on-call onboarding that includes runbook walkthroughs and a supervised shadow rotation.
- Each team owning production services must maintain at least 3 documented runbooks for critical failure modes.

Escalation Playbook (quick cheatsheet)

1) Confirm: verify alert signal and scope.
2) Contain: apply short-term mitigations (traffic routing, throttles, rollbacks).
3) Communicate: open incident channel and post initial status.
4) Escalate: if unable to mitigate within target timeframe escalate to secondary/on-call manager.
5) Recover: restore service, validate, and monitor.
6) Remediate: open follow-up tickets and schedule postmortem.
